requirements.requirement: The system should respond to parts search queries within 15 seconds.
requirements.source_citation: Honestly, it just needs to feel fast. But if you want a number, I guess for the parts search anything longer than, um, say fifteen seconds feels like forever
requirements.rationale: The stakeholder explicitly states a performance requirement for parts search, providing a clear timeframe of 15 seconds.
requirements.follow_up_question: Are there specific parts search scenarios or data volumes that would require different performance targets?

requirements.requirement: The system should respond to facility search queries within 8 seconds.
requirements.source_citation: For finding a preferred repair facility, I expect it to be quicker—maybe eight seconds is reasonable
requirements.rationale: The stakeholder explicitly states a performance requirement for facility search, providing a clear timeframe of 8 seconds.
requirements.follow_up_question: Are there specific facility search scenarios or data volumes that would require different performance targets?

requirements.requirement: The system should generate audit reports within 10 seconds.
requirements.source_citation: The audit report needs to be something I can get before I move on. If I have to wait more than, hmm, ten seconds it interrupts my flow
requirements.rationale: The stakeholder explicitly states a performance requirement for audit report generation, providing a clear timeframe of 10 seconds.
requirements.follow_up_question: Are there specific audit report scenarios or data volumes that would require different performance targets?

requirements.requirement: The system should maintain performance under load, supporting multiple concurrent users, especially during peak times like lunch rushes.
requirements.source_citation: When I'm in the office multiple adjusters are using it at once and it needs to keep up. Oh, and I forgot to mention, there's usually a lunch rush where everybody's trying to pull parts at the same time
requirements.rationale: The stakeholder explicitly mentions the need for the system to handle multiple concurrent users and peak usage times.
requirements.follow_up_question: What is the expected number of concurrent users during peak times, and what specific performance metrics should be maintained?

requirements.requirement: The system should provide in-context help on at least 90% of screens to assist users without leaving their current task.
requirements.source_citation: It should be almost everywhere, like, you know, if I'm stuck I should be able to find guidance right where I'm working, not have to go to some separate manual. If I had to guess, maybe help should be available in the vast majority of screens—so users don't get stuck. I mean, ninety percent of the system having in-context help would be brilliant.
requirements.rationale: The stakeholder explicitly states the need for in-context help on most screens, providing a clear target of 90% of the system.
requirements.follow_up_question: What specific types of help or guidance should be provided in-context, and how should this help be triggered or accessed?

requirements.requirement: The system should require minimal training time, with most users able to learn the basics quickly and within two days of onsite training.
requirements.source_citation: It can't be one of those big, drawn-out trainings. Most folks are busy, so it should be short and practical, done onsite with hands-on stuff. I'd say two days of onsite training should get people comfortable, but it should also be obvious enough that people pickup the basics quickly.
requirements.rationale: The stakeholder explicitly states the need for minimal training time, providing a clear target of two days of onsite training.
requirements.follow_up_question: What specific aspects of the system should be covered in the training, and what metrics will be used to assess user proficiency?

requirements.requirement: The system should integrate directly with the Choice Parts data feed to ensure real-time availability and prevent manual updates or exports.
requirements.source_citation: If it doesn't tap into the Choice Parts data directly we'll end up with old availability all the time. I mean, I've been on a call with a shop where they said a part was in stock, but our system didn't show it because someone forgot to update an export. That kills trust. So it needs to use the same feed we rely on now.
requirements.rationale: The stakeholder explicitly states the need for direct integration with the Choice Parts data feed to ensure real-time availability and prevent manual updates or exports.
requirements.follow_up_question: What specific data fields or updates should be synchronized with the Choice Parts data feed, and what processes should be in place to handle feed failures or discrepancies?

requirements.requirement: The system should adhere to the company's UI guidelines to ensure consistency with other corporate applications and minimize user confusion.
requirements.source_citation: If the layout, colors, and controls are different from our other corporate apps people get confused and make mistakes. It should feel like one of our apps so it's intuitive. Also, for compliance and branding it's just easier if it's consistent.
requirements.rationale: The stakeholder explicitly states the need for adherence to the company's UI guidelines to ensure consistency and minimize user confusion.
requirements.follow_up_question: What specific UI guidelines or design systems should the system adhere to, and how will compliance be validated?

requirements.requirement: The system should have an uptime of at least 98% to ensure reliability and minimize downtime.
requirements.source_citation: It needs to be reliable almost all the time. If it's down frequently people can't do their job. If you're asking for a metric, I'd say we need it up almost always, with very little downtime—maybe around ninety-eight percent uptime would be acceptable. But honestly, the less downtime the better.
requirements.rationale: The stakeholder explicitly states the need for high uptime, providing a clear target of 98%.
requirements.follow_up_question: What specific availability targets should be set for different times of the day or week, and what processes should be in place to handle downtime or outages?

requirements.requirement: The system should be forgiving, allowing users to easily undo or correct mistakes.
requirements.source_citation: It should be forgiving. People make mistakes, so undo or easy corrections are nice.
requirements.rationale: The stakeholder explicitly states the need for the system to be forgiving, allowing users to easily undo or correct mistakes.
requirements.follow_up_question: What specific types of mistakes or corrections should the system support, and how should these features be implemented or triggered?

requirements.requirement: The system should provide notifications when a part's status changes.
requirements.source_citation: Notifications when a part changes status would be good, because I don't want to keep checking.
requirements.rationale: The stakeholder explicitly states the need for notifications when a part's status changes.
requirements.follow_up_question: What specific part status changes should trigger notifications, and how should these notifications be delivered or displayed?

requirements.requirement: The system should function effectively in various environments, including those with limited connectivity or unusual usage contexts.
requirements.source_citation: Sometimes I go off on a tangent when I'm grabbing parts at lunch, like I once ended up negotiating prices while eating my sandwich, which was, um, maybe not efficient, but it shows we need the tool to work in weird spots.
requirements.rationale: The stakeholder implicitly suggests the need for the system to function effectively in various environments, including those with limited connectivity or unusual usage contexts.
requirements.follow_up_question: What specific environments or usage contexts should the system support, and what performance or functionality targets should be set for these scenarios?

requirements.requirement: The system should prevent users from accessing claims or customer details from other insurance companies.
requirements.source_citation: We absolutely cannot see another insurance company's claims. That would be a nightmare. Each company needs its own space so claims and customer details are private.
requirements.rationale: The stakeholder explicitly states the need for the system to prevent users from accessing claims or customer details from other insurance companies.
requirements.follow_up_question: What specific security measures or access controls should be implemented to prevent unauthorized access to claims or customer details from other insurance companies?

requirements.requirement: The system should implement role-based access control to ensure users can only access data and functionality relevant to their role.
requirements.source_citation: Within a company, people should see different things depending on their role—some folks need full view, others only the basics.
requirements.rationale: The stakeholder explicitly states the need for the system to implement role-based access control to ensure users can only access data and functionality relevant to their role.
requirements.follow_up_question: What specific roles or user groups should be defined, and what data or functionality should each role have access to?
